subs.title: Locus and Problems with Other Conics

questions.q: The locus of a variable point whose distance from \((-2,0)\) is \(2/3\) times its distance from the line \(x=-\dfrac92\) is
questions.sol: Focus–directrix definition with eccentricity \(\dfrac23<1\).

questions.q: Let \(E\) be the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) and \(C\) be the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\). Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the points \((1,2)\) and \((2,1)\) respectively. Then
questions.sol: \(P\): \(\dfrac19+1>1\) (outside \(E\)), \(1+4<9\) (inside \(C\)). \(Q\): \(\dfrac49+\dfrac14<1\) (inside \(E\)) and inside \(C\).

questions.q: The radius of the circle passing through the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\), and having its centre at \((0,3)\) is
questions.sol: Foci \((\pm\sqrt7,0)\); radius \(=\sqrt{7+9}\).

questions.q: If \(P=(x,y)\) be any point on \(16x^2+25y^2=400\) with foci \(F_1=(3,0)\), \(F_2=(-3,0)\) then \(PF_1+PF_2\) equals
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\): the sum of focal distances is \(2a=10\).

questions.q: The area of the quadrilateral formed by the tangents at the end points of latus rectum to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}5=1\), is
questions.sol: \(e=\dfrac23\). Tangent at \(\left(2,\dfrac53\right)\): \(\dfrac{2x}9+\dfrac y3=1\), intercepts \(\dfrac92\) and \(3\). Area of the rhombus \(=4\cdot\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac92\cdot3\).

questions.q: If tangents are drawn to the ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=2\), then the locus of the midpoint of the intercept made by the tangents between the coordinate axes is
questions.sol: Tangent \(\dfrac{x\cos\theta}{\sqrt2}+y\sin\theta=1\) has intercepts \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\cos\theta},\dfrac1{\sin\theta}\). Mid point: \(\cos\theta=\dfrac1{\sqrt2h}\), \(\sin\theta=\dfrac1{2k}\).

questions.q: The line passing through the extremity \(A\) of the major axis and extremity \(B\) of the minor axis of the ellipse \(x^2+9y^2=9\) meets its auxiliary circle at the point \(M\). Then the area of the triangle with vertices at \(A\), \(M\) and the origin \(O\) is

The normal at a point \(P\) on the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=16\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\). If \(M\) is the mid point of the line segment \(PQ\), then the locus of \(M\) intersects the latus rectum of the given ellipse at the points
questions.sol: \(P(4\cos\theta,2\sin\theta)\); normal \(4x\sec\theta-2y\,\text{cosec}\,\theta=12\) gives \(Q(3\cos\theta,0)\). \(M=\left(\dfrac72\cos\theta,\sin\theta\right)\): \(\dfrac{4x^2}{49}+y^2=1\). On \(x=\pm ae=\pm2\sqrt3\): \(y^2=\dfrac1{49}\).

questions.q: The ellipse \(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) is inscribed in a rectangle \(R\) whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes. Another ellipse \(E_2\) passing through the point \((0,4)\) circumscribes the rectangle \(R\). The eccentricity of the ellipse \(E_2\) is

Let \(a,b\) and \(\lambda\) be positive real numbers. Suppose \(P\) is an end point of the latus rectum of the parabola \(y^2=4\lambda x\), and suppose the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) passes through the point \(P\). If the tangents to the parabola and the ellipse at the point \(P\) are perpendicular to each other, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.sol: \(P=(\lambda,2\lambda)\): slope of the parabola's tangent is \(1\); of the ellipse's, \(-\dfrac{b^2x}{a^2y}=-\dfrac{b^2}{2a^2}=-1\). So \(b^2=2a^2\) and \(e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{a^2}{b^2}}\).

questions.q: Consider the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\). Let \(S(p,q)\) be a point in the first quadrant such that \(\dfrac{p^2}9+\dfrac{q^2}4>1\). Two tangents are drawn from \(S\) to the ellipse, of which one meets the ellipse at one end point of the minor axis and the other meets the ellipse at a point \(T\) in the fourth quadrant. Let \(R\) be the vertex of the ellipse with positive \(x\)-coordinate and \(O\) be the center of the ellipse. If the area of the triangle \(\Delta ORT\) is \(\dfrac32\), then which of the following options is correct?
questions.sol: The tangent at \((0,2)\) is \(y=2\), so \(q=2\). \(\dfrac12\cdot3\cdot|y_T|=\dfrac32\): \(T=\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,-1\right)\). Tangent at \(T\): \(\dfrac{\sqrt3x}6-\dfrac y4=1\); at \(y=2\): \(x=3\sqrt3\).

questions.q: On the ellipse \(4x^2+9y^2=1\), the points at which the tangents are parallel to the line \(8x=9y\) are
questions.sol: Slope \(-\dfrac{4x}{9y}=\dfrac89\) gives \(x=-2y\); then \(25y^2=1\).

questions.q: Let \(P(x_1,y_1)\) and \(Q(x_2,y_2)\), \(y_1<0\), \(y_2<0\), be the end points of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\). The equations of parabolas with latus rectum \(PQ\) are
questions.sol: \(P,Q=\left(\pm\sqrt3,-\dfrac12\right)\): focus \(\left(0,-\dfrac12\right)\), \(4A=2\sqrt3\). Vertex \(\left(0,-\dfrac12\mp\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)\): \(x^2=2\sqrt3\left(y+\dfrac12+\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)\) or \(x^2=-2\sqrt3\left(y+\dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) be two ellipses whose centres are at the origin. The major axes of \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) lie along the \(x\)-axis and the \(y\)-axis respectively. Let \(S\) be the circle \(x^2+(y-1)^2=2\). The straight line \(x+y=3\) touches the curves \(S\), \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) at \(P,Q\) and \(R\), respectively. Suppose that \(PQ=PR=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}3\). If \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) are the eccentricities of \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) respectively, then the correct expression(s) is(are)

Consider two straight lines, each of which is tangent to both the circle \(x^2+y^2=\dfrac12\) and the parabola \(y^2=4x\). Let these lines intersect at the point \(Q\). Consider the ellipse whose center is at the origin \(O(0,0)\) and whose semi-major axis is \(OQ\). If the length of the minor axis of this ellipse is \(\sqrt2\), then which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
opts: For the ellipse, the eccentricity is \(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) and the length of the latus rectum is \(1\)
For the ellipse, the eccentricity is \(\dfrac12\) and the length of the latus rectum is \(\dfrac12\)
The area of the region bounded by the ellipse between the lines \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) and \(x=1\) is \(\dfrac1{4\sqrt2}(\pi-2)\)
The area of the region bounded by the ellipse between the lines \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) and \(x=1\) is \(\dfrac1{16}(\pi-2)\)
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac1m\) touches the circle when \(m^4+m^2-2=0\): \(y=\pm(x+1)\), \(Q=(-1,0)\). Ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=1\): \(e=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\), latus rectum \(\dfrac{2b^2}a=1\). Area \(=\sqrt2\displaystyle\int_{1/\sqrt2}^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx=\sqrt2\left(\dfrac\pi8-\dfrac14\right)\).

questions.q:
Define the collections \(\{E_1,E_2,E_3,\ldots\}\) of ellipses and \(\{R_1,R_2,R_3,\ldots\}\) of rectangles as follows :
\(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\);
\(R_1\) : rectangle of largest area, with sides parallel to the axes, inscribed in \(E_1\);
\(E_n\) : ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a_n^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b_n^2}=1\) of largest area inscribed in \(R_{n-1}\), \(n>1\);
\(R_n\) : rectangle of largest area, with sides parallel to the axes, inscribed in \(E_n\), \(n>1\).
Then which of the following options is/are correct?
opts: The eccentricities of \(E_{18}\) and \(E_{19}\) are NOT equal.
The length of latus rectum of \(E_9\) is \(\dfrac16\).
The distance of a focus from the centre in \(E_9\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}{32}\).
questions.sol: The largest rectangle in an ellipse has half-sides \(\dfrac a{\sqrt2},\dfrac b{\sqrt2}\) (area \(2ab\)), which become the semi-axes of the next ellipse: \(a_n=\dfrac3{(\sqrt2)^{n-1}}\), \(b_n=\dfrac2{(\sqrt2)^{n-1}}\). All eccentricities equal \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}3\). \(E_9\): \(a=\dfrac3{16}\), \(b=\dfrac18\): latus rectum \(\dfrac16\), \(ae=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{16}\). Areas \(\dfrac{12}{2^{n-1}}\) sum to less than \(24\).

questions.q: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) be two distinct common tangents to the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}6+\dfrac{y^2}3=1\) and the parabola \(P:y^2=12x\). Suppose that the tangent \(T_1\) touches \(P\) and \(E\) at the points \(A_1\) and \(A_2\), respectively and the tangent \(T_2\) touches \(P\) and \(E\) at the points \(A_4\) and \(A_3\), respectively. Then which of the following statements is (are) true?
opts: The area of the quadrilateral \(A_1A_2A_3A_4\) is \(35\) square units
The area of the quadrilateral \(A_1A_2A_3A_4\) is \(36\) square units
The tangents \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) meet the \(x\)-axis at the point \((-3,0)\)
The tangents \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) meet the \(x\)-axis at the point \((-6,0)\)
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac3m\) touches \(E\) when \(\dfrac9{m^2}=6m^2+3\): \(m=\pm1\), \(y=\pm(x+3)\). Contact points: \((3,\pm6)\) on \(P\), \((-2,\pm1)\) on \(E\). Trapezium with parallel sides \(12\), \(2\) and height \(5\).

questions.q: Let \(d\) be the perpendicular distance from the centre of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) to the tangent drawn at a point \(P\) on the ellipse. If \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are the two foci of the ellipse then show that \((PF_1-PF_2)^2=4a^2\left(1-\dfrac{b^2}{d^2}\right)\).
questions.sol: For \(P(a\cos\theta,b\sin\theta)\): \(PF_{1,2}=a\mp ae\cos\theta\), so \((PF_1-PF_2)^2=4a^2e^2\cos^2\theta\). Also \(\dfrac1{d^2}=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{a^2}+\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{b^2}\), so \(1-\dfrac{b^2}{d^2}=\cos^2\theta\left(1-\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}\right)=e^2\cos^2\theta\).

questions.q: A tangent to the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\) meets the ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=6\) at \(P\) and \(Q\). Prove that the tangents at \(P\) and \(Q\) of the ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=6\) are at right angles.
questions.sol: Tangent to the first ellipse: \(\dfrac{x\cos\theta}2+y\sin\theta=1\). If the tangents at \(P,Q\) meet at \((h,k)\), \(PQ\) is \(\dfrac{hx}6+\dfrac{ky}3=1\). Comparing: \(h=3\cos\theta\), \(k=3\sin\theta\), so \(h^2+k^2=9=6+3\) — the point lies on the director circle of \(\dfrac{x^2}6+\dfrac{y^2}3=1\).

questions.q: Find the coordinates of all points \(P\) on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), for which the area of the triangle \(PON\) is maximum, where \(O\) denotes the origin and \(N\), the foot of the perpendicular from \(O\) to the tangent at \(P\).
questions.sol: For \(P(a\cos\theta,b\sin\theta)\): \(ON=\dfrac{ab}{\sqrt{a^2\sin^2\theta+b^2\cos^2\theta}}\), \(PN=\dfrac{(a^2-b^2)|\sin\theta\cos\theta|}{\sqrt{a^2\sin^2\theta+b^2\cos^2\theta}}\). Area \(=\dfrac{ab(a^2-b^2)}{2\left(a^2|\tan\theta|+b^2|\cot\theta|\right)}\), greatest when \(a^2|\tan\theta|=b^2|\cot\theta|\), i.e. \(\tan\theta=\pm\dfrac ba\).

questions.q: Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle \(x^2+y^2=a^2\), suppose perpendiculars from \(A,B,C\) to the major axis of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\); \((a>b)\) meet the ellipse respectively at \(P,Q,R\) so that \(P,Q,R\) on the same side of the major axis as \(A,B,C\) respectively. Prove that the normals to the ellipse drawn at the points \(P,Q\) and \(R\) are concurrent.
questions.sol: \(P,Q,R\) have eccentric angles \(\phi_i=\theta+\dfrac{2\pi i}3\) \((i=0,1,2)\). Normal at \(\phi\): \(ax\sin\phi-by\cos\phi=\dfrac{a^2-b^2}2\sin2\phi\). Since \(\sum\sin\phi_i=\sum\cos\phi_i=\sum\sin2\phi_i=0\), the three equations add up to \(0=0\): they are linearly dependent, so the three (non-parallel) normals are concurrent.

questions.q: Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be two circles with \(C_2\) lying inside \(C_1\). A circle \(C\) lying inside \(C_1\) touches \(C_1\) internally and \(C_2\) externally. Identify the locus of the centre of \(C\).
questions.ans: Ellipse (with foci at the centres of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\))
questions.sol: If \(C\) has centre \(O\) and radius \(r\): \(OO_1=r_1-r\) and \(OO_2=r_2+r\), so \(OO_1+OO_2=r_1+r_2\), a constant.

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(0<b<a\). Let the line parallel to \(y\)-axis, passing through \(P\) meets the circle \(x^2+y^2=a^2\) at the point \(Q\) such that \(P\) and \(Q\) are on the same side of \(x\)-axis. For two positive real numbers \(r\) and \(s\), find the locus of the point \(R\) on \(PQ\) such that \(PR:RQ=r:s\) and \(P\) varies over the ellipse.
questions.sol: \(P=(a\cos\theta,b\sin\theta)\), \(Q=(a\cos\theta,a\sin\theta)\), \(R=\left(a\cos\theta,\dfrac{(sb+ra)\sin\theta}{r+s}\right)\). Eliminate \(\theta\).

questions.q: Prove that in an ellipse, the perpendicular from a focus upon any tangent and the line joining the centre of the ellipse to the point of contact meet on the corresponding directrix.
questions.sol: Tangent at \(P(a\cos\theta,b\sin\theta)\) has slope \(-\dfrac{b\cos\theta}{a\sin\theta}\). Perpendicular from \((ae,0)\): \(y=\dfrac{a\sin\theta}{b\cos\theta}(x-ae)\); line \(CP\): \(y=\dfrac{b\sin\theta}{a\cos\theta}x\). Equating: \(x\left(\dfrac ab-\dfrac ba\right)=\dfrac{a^2e}b\), so \(x=\dfrac{a^3e}{a^2-b^2}=\dfrac ae\).

questions.q: Find the equation of the common tangent in \(1^{st}\) quadrant to the circle \(x^2+y^2=16\) and the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\). Also find the length of the intercept of the tangent between the coordinates axes.
questions.sol: \(y=mx+c\) with \(c^2=16(1+m^2)=25m^2+4\): \(m^2=\dfrac43\), \(c^2=\dfrac{112}3\); in the first quadrant \(m<0\). Intercepts \(\dfrac c{|m|}=2\sqrt7\) and \(c\): length \(\sqrt{28+\dfrac{112}3}\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a variable point on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). With foci \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). If \(A\) is the area of the triangle \(PF_1F_2\) then maximum value of \(A\) is ............
questions.sol: Base \(F_1F_2=2ae\), greatest height \(b\): \(A_{\max}=abe\).

questions.q: An ellipse has \(OB\) as a semi minor axis. \(F,F'\) are its foci, and the angle \(FBF'\) is a right angle. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is..................

Consider the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}3=1\)
Let \(H(\alpha,0)\), \(0<\alpha<2\), be a point. A straight line drawn through \(H\) parallel to the \(y\)-axis crosses the ellipse and its auxiliary circle at points \(E\) and \(F\) respectively, in the first quadrant. The tangent to the ellipse at the point \(E\) intersects the positive \(x\)-axis at a point \(G\). Suppose the straight line joining \(F\) and the origin makes an angle \(\phi\) with the positive \(x\)-axis.
List-IList-II
(I) If \(\phi=\dfrac\pi4\), then the area of the triangle \(FGH\) is(P) \(\dfrac{(\sqrt3-1)^4}8\)
(II) If \(\phi=\dfrac\pi3\), then the area of the triangle \(FGH\) is(Q) \(1\)
(III) If \(\phi=\dfrac\pi6\), then the area of the triangle \(FGH\) is(R) \(\dfrac34\)
(IV) If \(\phi=\dfrac\pi{12}\), then the area of the triangle \(FGH\) is(S) \(\dfrac1{2\sqrt3}\)
(T) \(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2\)
The correct option is :
questions.sol: \(F=(2\cos\phi,2\sin\phi)\), \(H=(2\cos\phi,0)\), \(G=\left(\dfrac2{\cos\phi},0\right)\). Area \(=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac2{\cos\phi}-2\cos\phi\right)2\sin\phi=\dfrac{2\sin^3\phi}{\cos\phi}\): values \(1\), \(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2\), \(\dfrac1{2\sqrt3}\) and (for \(15^\circ\)) \(\dfrac{(\sqrt3-1)^3}{4(\sqrt3+1)}=\dfrac{(\sqrt3-1)^4}8\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Tangents are drawn from the point \(P(3,4)\) to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) touching the ellipse at points \(A\) and \(B\).
The coordinates of \(A\) and \(B\) are
questions.sol: Chord of contact: \(\dfrac x3+y=1\). Putting \(x=3-3y\) in the ellipse: \((1-y)^2+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\), \(y=0\) or \(\dfrac85\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Tangents are drawn from the point \(P(3,4)\) to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) touching the ellipse at points \(A\) and \(B\).
The orthocentre of the triangle \(PAB\) is
questions.sol: \(A(3,0)\), \(B\left(-\dfrac95,\dfrac85\right)\). \(PA\) is the line \(x=3\), so the altitude from \(B\) is \(y=\dfrac85\). \(PB\) has slope \(\dfrac12\); altitude from \(A\): \(y=-2(x-3)\). They meet at \(x=\dfrac{11}5\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Tangents are drawn from the point \(P(3,4)\) to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) touching the ellipse at points \(A\) and \(B\).
The equation of the locus of the point whose distances from the point \(P\) and the line \(AB\) are equal, is

Comprehension
Let \(F_1(x_1,0)\) and \(F_2(x_2,0)\), for \(x_1<0\) and \(x_2>0\), be the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}8=1\). Suppose a parabola having vertex at the origin and focus at \(F_2\) intersects the ellipse at point \(M\) in the first quadrant and at point \(N\) in the fourth quadrant.
The orthocentre of the triangle \(F_1MN\) is
questions.sol: \(e=\dfrac13\): \(F_1=(-1,0)\), \(F_2=(1,0)\), parabola \(y^2=4x\). \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac x2=1\) gives \(x=\dfrac32\): \(M=\left(\dfrac32,\sqrt6\right)\), \(N=\left(\dfrac32,-\sqrt6\right)\). One altitude is the \(x\)-axis. \(F_1N\) has slope \(-\dfrac{2\sqrt6}5\); the altitude from \(M\), \(y-\sqrt6=\dfrac5{2\sqrt6}\left(x-\dfrac32\right)\), meets \(y=0\) at \(x=\dfrac32-\dfrac{12}5\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(F_1(x_1,0)\) and \(F_2(x_2,0)\), for \(x_1<0\) and \(x_2>0\), be the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}8=1\). Suppose a parabola having vertex at the origin and focus at \(F_2\) intersects the ellipse at point \(M\) in the first quadrant and at point \(N\) in the fourth quadrant.
If the tangents to the ellipse at \(M\) and \(N\) meet at \(R\) and the normal to the parabola at \(M\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\), then the ratio of area of the triangle \(MQR\) to area of the quadrilateral \(MF_1NF_2\) is
questions.sol: \(e=\dfrac13\): \(F_1=(-1,0)\), \(F_2=(1,0)\), parabola \(y^2=4x\). \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac x2=1\) gives \(x=\dfrac32\): \(M=\left(\dfrac32,\sqrt6\right)\), \(N=\left(\dfrac32,-\sqrt6\right)\). Tangent at \(M\): \(\dfrac x6+\dfrac{\sqrt6y}8=1\), so \(R=(6,0)\). Normal to the parabola at \(M\) (slope \(-\dfrac{\sqrt6}2\)) gives \(Q=\left(\dfrac72,0\right)\). Area \(MQR=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac52\cdot\sqrt6\); area \(MF_1NF_2=\dfrac12\cdot2\cdot2\sqrt6\).

questions.q: Suppose that the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}5=1\) are \((f_1,0)\) and \((f_2,0)\) where \(f_1>0\) and \(f_2<0\). Let \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) be two parabolas with a common vertex at \((0,0)\) and with foci at \((f_1,0)\) and \((2f_2,0)\) respectively. Let \(T_1\) be a tangent to \(P_1\) which passes through \((2f_2,0)\) and \(T_2\) be a tangent to \(P_2\) which passes through \((f_1,0)\). If \(m_1\) is the slope of \(T_1\) and \(m_2\) is the slope of \(T_2\), then the value of \(\left(\dfrac1{m_1^2}+m_2^2\right)\) is

Let \(E\) be the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\). For any three distinct points \(P,Q\) and \(Q'\) on \(E\), let \(M(P,Q)\) be the mid-point of the line segment joining \(P\) and \(Q\), and \(M(P,Q')\) be the mid-point of the line segment joining \(P\) and \(Q'\). Then the maximum possible value of the distance between \(M(P,Q)\) and \(M(P,Q')\), as \(P,Q\) and \(Q'\) vary on \(E\), is ______.
questions.sol: The distance between the mid points is \(\dfrac12QQ'\), and the longest chord of the ellipse is the major axis, \(8\).

questions.q:
Let \(P(x_1,y_1)\) and \(Q(x_2,y_2)\) be two distinct points on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) such that \(y_1>0\), and \(y_2>0\). Let \(C\) denote the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\), and \(M\) be the point \((3,0)\).
Suppose the line \(x=x_1\) intersects \(C\) at \(R\), and the line \(x=x_2\) intersects \(C\) at \(S\), such that the \(y\)-coordinates of \(R\) and \(S\) are positive. Let \(\angle ROM=\dfrac\pi6\) and \(\angle SOM=\dfrac\pi3\), where \(O\) denotes the origin \((0,0)\). Let \(|XY|\) denote the length of the line segment \(XY\).
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: The equation of the line joining \(P\) and \(Q\) is \(2x+3y=3(1+\sqrt3)\)
The equation of the line joining \(P\) and \(Q\) is \(2x+y=3(1+\sqrt3)\)
questions.sol: \(C\) is the auxiliary circle: \(P=\left(3\cos\dfrac\pi6,2\sin\dfrac\pi6\right)=\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,1\right)\), \(Q=\left(\dfrac32,\sqrt3\right)\). Slope of \(PQ=-\dfrac23\): \(2x+3y=3+3\sqrt3\). Ordinates on the ellipse are \(\dfrac23\) of those on the circle: \(3|N_2Q|=2|N_2S|\) and \(3|N_1P|=2|N_1R|\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Consider the ellipses given by \(x^2+4y^2=1\) and \(4x^2+y^2=1\).
Let \(P\) be the point in the first quadrant where the given ellipses intersect. If \(\theta\) is the acute angle between the tangents to the given ellipses at the point \(P\), then the value of \(4\tan\theta\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(P=\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt5},\dfrac1{\sqrt5}\right)\). Slopes there: \(-\dfrac x{4y}=-\dfrac14\) and \(-\dfrac{4x}y=-4\). \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{4-\frac14}{1+1}=\dfrac{15}8\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Consider the ellipses given by \(x^2+4y^2=1\) and \(4x^2+y^2=1\).
If \(\alpha\) is the area of the common region that lies inside both the given ellipses, then the value of \(\cot\alpha\) is ______.
questions.sol: By symmetry the area is \(8\) times the part with polar angle in \(\left[0,\dfrac\pi4\right]\), bounded there by \(4x^2+y^2=1\): \(\alpha=8\cdot\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{d\phi}{4\cos^2\phi+\sin^2\phi}=4\cdot\dfrac12\tan^{-1}\dfrac12=2\tan^{-1}\dfrac12\). So \(\tan\alpha=\dfrac43\).
